question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer must access a Cisco UCS C-Series server KVM from a remote location. The engineer must use the out-of-band interface to access the KVM. Which configuration set meets these requirements?
context:
Topology: Server MGMT/LAN1/LAN2 connect to switch ports E1/0/10, E1/0/11, E1/0/12.
interface Ethernet1/0/10
  switchport mode access
  switchport access vlan 100
interface Ethernet1/0/11
  switchport mode access
  switchport access vlan 101
interface Ethernet1/0/12
  switchport mode access
  switchport access vlan 102
imageNote: Diagram: server MGMT/LAN1/LAN2 ports connect to switch ports E1/0/10, E1/0/11, E1/0/12 respectively.
options: NIC mode: Shared LOM - VLAN ID: 100
NIC mode: Dedicated - VLAN state: Disabled
NIC mode: Shared LOM - VLAN state: Disabled
theory: Accessing a C-Series server's KVM through the dedicated out-of-band management interface requires setting Cisco IMC's NIC mode to Dedicated (not Shared LOM, which multiplexes management traffic over a data NIC). Because the upstream switch port for that management interface is configured as an untagged access port (switchport mode access) rather than a VLAN trunk, the Cisco IMC VLAN tagging state must be Disabled to match — enabling and tagging a VLAN ID on the CIMC side when the switch port expects untagged traffic would break connectivity rather than restrict it correctly. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco IMC Network Management, Dedicated NIC Mode)
